fields.title: 📖 Recovering a right is not automatically Shirk Akbar
fields.body:
🖋️ **al-Māwardī** said about recovering a withheld right:

> ***“One of the two forms is that he is able to take his right from him through Muḥākamah.”***

This statement does not stand in a chapter on Shirk, but in the Fiqh chapter on taking one’s own right from someone who withholds it.

🖋️ The Fuqahāʾ likewise distinguished between the forbidden seeking of the Ṭāġūt judgment and the repelling of wrong, or the recovery of one’s own right.

> ***A complaint, a lawsuit, or a demand for return is not automatically Kufr Akbar or Shirk Akbar, so long as one does not take Bāṭil and does not prefer the Ṭāġūt judgment to the judgment of Allah.***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The direct Ṭāġūt text condemns the intended Ṭāġūt judgment and Riḍā with it instead of with the judgment of Allah. The recovery of a withheld right, by contrast, was treated by the Fuqahāʾ as its own subject of Fiqh: **Muḥākamah, Daʿāwā, Bayyināt, Aḫdh al-Ḥaqq, and Dafʿ aẓ-Ẓulm**.
